claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys can possess a nanocrystalline microstructure with uniformly small grains and a high density of grain boundaries.
A high density of grain boundaries facilitates distributed nucleation during the magnetostructural transition.
Distributed nucleation makes the first-order magnetostructural phase change smoother and less abrupt.
The smoother phase change reduces hysteresis and broadens the entropy-change response.
Reduced hysteresis and a broadened entropy response enhance the efficiency of low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type baseline films have a relatively coarse, unoptimized grain structure.
Sputter-deposited multicomponent films can be prepared on Si-based substrates.
Tailoring sputter deposition can produce 50–200 nm FeMnNiGeSi-type films with controlled, uniformly nanocrystalline grain sizes.
TEM and in-plane XRD stress mapping can verify grain-size uniformity and detrimental residual stress immediately after deposition.
Deposition on Si at approximately 400°C will provide high crystallinity in the FeMnNiGeSi-type films.
Rapid cooling after deposition will lock in the desired nanostructure.
Nanocrystalline grains provide an enhanced surface-to-volume ratio and a high density of grain boundaries.
Grain boundaries reduce local transformation-energy barriers and distribute the phase transformation over a broader temperature range.
The proposed grain-boundary mechanism can reduce hysteresis without significantly compromising the magnetocaloric effect.
Nanocrystalline films will have a broader magnetostructural transition and lower hysteretic losses than films with larger or inhomogeneous grains.
Nanocrystalline films will enable more efficient heat exchange while retaining a useful magnetocaloric response.
Bulk or conventionally sputtered coarse-grained FeMnNiGeSi-type materials undergo a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with high hysteresis and limited heat-exchange rates.
The predictions should hold for 50–200 nm films under low-field cooling cycles provided intrinsic magnetic ordering and thermal management are maintained.
Excessive grain refinement or microstructural inhomogeneity may reduce the magnetocaloric amplitude.

contradictions.description: The mechanism and uncertainty fields allow a slight or controlled reduction in magnetocaloric amplitude, whereas the falsification rule states that an adversely affected magnetocaloric effect is sufficient for rejection without defining how much reduction counts as adverse.
